Elena — thanks for the clear list. I put together a concise annex and a working draft of an incident notification template attached (incident-comms-draft.pdf) and a single-sheet TAM coverage table (NSB-RFI-TAM_table_v1.xlsx). Key highlights below; full details are attached.

- TAM model: Customers are assigned a named TAM (business hours) and a 24/7 on-call rotation for Sev1 escalations. Primary on-call covers first 4 hours; secondary rotates in at 4 hours and remains until handoff. 
- Response targets: Sev1 — initial triage within 30 minutes (24/7); Sev2 — initial contact within 2 hours (24/7); Sev3/4 — next business day. We include timestamps and acknowledgement in every notification.
- Notification SLAs: initial customer admin notification within 30 minutes of confirmed Sev1; status page updated within 1 hour; interim updates every 2 hours until resolution for Sev1.
- Channels: PagerDuty for on-call, email to configured customer admin list, and optional dedicated Slack channel. We support webhook and OOB PagerDuty integration; customers can opt for SMS for critical P1s.
- Cross-region: If a region-specific failover is triggered, we tag notifications with region and affected capacity; failover incidents may have an extended validation period but maintain the same initial notify SLA.

Please review the attached annex. Marissa — looping you in for any operational clarifications; Ben/Neha, see the proposed notification cadence and the small wording tweaks we might need for customers in regulated sectors.

Thanks,
